And whoever goes astray only goes astray to his own detriment meaning the consequences of that will only return to himself. And you are not a guardian over them meaning the one entrusted with ensuring that they are guided. You are only a warner, and God is, over all things, Disposer of affairs. “Upon you is only the conveyance, and upon Us is the account.” Then the Almighty said, informing about His noble self that He is the One who controls existence as He wills and that He takes souls by the greater death by sending guardians to seize them from the bodies, and the lesser death during sleep, as the Blessed and Exalted said: “And it is He who takes you by night and knows what you have committed by day. Then He raises you up therein that a specified term may be fulfilled. Then to Him is your return. Then He will inform you of what you used to do. And He is the Prevailing over His servants. And whoever goes astray only goes astray to his own detriment meaning the consequences of that will only return to himself. You are only a warner, and God is, over all things, Disposer of affairs. “Upon you is only the conveyance, and upon Us is the account.” Then the Almighty said, informing about His noble self that He is the One who controls existence as He wills and that He takes souls by the greater death by sending guardians to seize them from the bodies, and the lesser death during sleep, as the Blessed and Exalted said: “And it is He who takes you by night and knows what you have committed by day. 39:43: God Almighty says, blaming the polytheists for taking intercessors besides God, namely the idols and rivals that they took of their own accord without any evidence or proof that prompted them to do so. They do not possess any power over any matter, nor do they have a mind with which to comprehend, nor a hearing with which to hear, nor a sight with which to see. Rather, they are inanimate objects much worse than animals. Then He said: Say, O Muhammad, to these people who claim that the intercessors they have taken for themselves with God Almighty, inform them that intercession is of no benefit with God except for whom He is pleased with and has given permission, so all of it is returned to Him. Who is he that can intercede with Him except by His permission? “To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth,” meaning He is the One who controls all of that. Then to Him you will be returned, meaning on the Day of Resurrection, He will judge between you with His justice and reward each one according to his deeds. Then God Almighty said, blaming the polytheists as well: And when God is mentioned alone, meaning when it is said, There is no god but God alone, “the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter are filled with disgust.” Mujahid said, They are filled with disgust and contract. And he said, Al-Suddi said: She was repelled. Qatada said: She disbelieved and was arrogant. Malik said on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam: She was arrogant, as God Almighty said: Indeed, when it was said to them, ‘There is no god but God,’ they were arrogant, meaning about following and submitting to it. Their hearts do not accept good, and whoever does not accept good accepts evil. Therefore God Almighty said: And when those other than Him are mentioned, meaning of the idols and rivals. Mujahid said: At once, they rejoice, meaning they are happy and pleased.

39:46: God the Most High says after mentioning the polytheists, what He mentioned of their condemnation for their love of polytheism and their aversion to monotheism: “Say: ‘O God, Creator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed.’” That is, call upon God alone, with no partner who created the heavens and the earth and originated them, that is, made them without a previous example. Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, that is, the secret and the public. You will judge between Your servants concerning that over which they used to differ. That is, in their worldly life, You will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection, their resurrection, and their rising from their graves. Muslim said in his Sahih: ‘Abd ibn Humayd told us, ‘Umar ibn Yunus told us, ‘Ikrimah ibn ‘Ammar told us, Yahya ibn Abi Katheer told us, Abu Salamah ibn ‘Abdur-Rahman told me: I asked Aisha may God be pleased with her: “How did the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) begin his prayer when he got up at night?” She, may God be pleased with her, said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, rose at night, he would begin his prayer by saying: “O God, Lord of Gabriel, Michael, and Israfil, Creator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, You judge between Your servants concerning that over which they differ. Guide me to the truth concerning that over which they differ, by Your permission. Indeed, You guide whom You will to a straight path.” Imam Ahmad said: Affan told us, Hammad bin Salamah told us, Suhayl told us, on the authority of Abu Salih and Abdullah bin Uthman bin Khathim, on the authority of Awn bin Abdullah bin Utbah bin Masoud, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever says: ‘O God, Creator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, I entrust You in this world that I bear witness that there is no god but God, You are alone, without partner, and that Muhammad is Your servant and Messenger. If You leave me to myself, You will bring me closer to evil and distance me from good. I trust only in Your mercy, so make for me a covenant with You that You will fulfill on the Day of Resurrection, for You do not fail to fulfill Your promise,’ except that the Almighty will say to His angels on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:‘My servant has entrusted Me with a covenant, so fulfill it, and God will admit him to Paradise.’” Suhayl said: I informed Al-Qasim bin Abd Al-Rahman that Awn had said such and such, so he said: There is no girl among us who does not say this in her chamber. This was narrated by Imam Ahmad alone, and Imam Ahmad said: Hasan told us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to me Huyayy ibn Abdullah that Abu Abdur-Rahman narrated to him that Abdullah ibn Amr may God be pleased with him brought out a piece of paper to us and said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) used to teach us to say: O God, Creator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, You are the Lord of all things and the God of all things. I bear witness that there is no god but You alone, without partner, and that Muhammad is Your servant and Messenger, and the angels bear witness. I seek refuge in You from Satan and his polytheism, and I seek refuge in You from committing a sin against myself or bringing one upon a Muslim. Abu Abdur-Rahman may God be pleased with him said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) taught Abdullah ibn Amr may God be pleased with him to say that when he wanted to sleep. Ahmad also narrated it alone. Imam Ahmad also said: Khalaf bin Al-Waleed told us, Ibn Ayyash told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ziyad Al-Alahani, on the authority of Abu Rashid Al-Hubrani, who said: I came to Abdullah bin Amr, may God be pleased with them both, and I said to him: Tell us what you heard from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He threw a scroll in front of me and said: This is what the Messenger of God wrote to me. I looked at it and it said that Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, said: O Messenger of God, teach me what to say when I wake up and when I go to bed. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: O Abu Bakr, say: O God, Creator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, there is no god but You, Lord of everything and its King. I seek refuge in You from the evil of my soul and the evil of Satan and his polytheism, or from committing evil against myself or bringing it upon a Muslim. Al-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Arfa, on the authority of Ismail bin Ayyash, and he said: It is good and strange from this chain of transmission. Imam Ahmad said: Hashim told us, Shaiban told us, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) commanded me to say when I wake up, when I go to bed at night, O God, Creator of the heavens and the earth, etc. And the words of God, the Exalted: And if those who do wrong - meaning the polytheists - had all that is on the earth and twice as much with it - meaning, even if they had all that is on the earth and double it with it, they would offer it as ransom from the evil of the punishment - meaning, what God has made obligatory for them on the Day of Resurrection. Despite this, the ransom will not be accepted from them, even if the earth was filled with gold, as He said in another verse: And there will appear to them from God that which they had never reckoned upon - meaning, there will appear to them from God a punishment and chastisement that they had not considered or calculated. And there will appear to them the evil of what they have earned - meaning, the recompense for what they earned in this world of forbidden acts and sins will appear to them. And that which they used to ridicule will encompass them - meaning, they will be surrounded by the punishment and chastisement that they used to ridicule in this world.

39:49: The Blessed and Exalted says, informing about man that when he is in distress, he supplicates to God Almighty, turns to Him, and calls upon Him. But if He grants him a blessing from Him, he transgresses and rebels, and says, It was only given to me because of knowledge, meaning because God Almighty knows that I deserve it. Had I not been special to God, He would not have granted me this. Qatada said, On the basis of knowledge I have, on the basis of information I have. God Almighty said, Rather, it is a trial, meaning the matter is not as he claimed. Rather, We only bestowed this blessing upon him to test him in what We have bestowed upon him, whether he would obey or disobey, despite Our prior knowledge of that. It is a trial, that is, a test. But most of them do not know, that is, they say what they say and claim what they claim. Those before them have already said it, meaning many of the nations who came before said this statement, claimed this assertion, and made this claim. So what they earned did not avail them, meaning their words were not true, nor did their gathering and what they earned prevent them. “So the evils of what they earned befell them. And those who…” Those who were wronged will be afflicted by the evils of what they earned, that is, just as those afflicted, and they will not escape, as God, the Most High, said, informing us about Qarun that his people said to him, “Do not rejoice. Indeed, God does not like the exultant. And seek, through that which God has given you, the home of the Hereafter, and do not forget your share of this world. And do good as God has been good to you, and do not seek corruption in the land. Indeed, God does not like corrupters.” He said, It has only been given to me because of knowledge I have. Did he not know that God destroyed before him generations who were stronger than him in strength and greater in multitude? And the criminals will not be asked about their sins. And God, the Most High, said, And they said, ‘We are more numerous in wealth and children, and we will not be punished.’ And God, the Most High, said, Do they not know that God expands provision for whom He wills and restricts it? That is, He expands it for some people and restricts it for others. Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe. That is, lessons and proofs.

39:53: This noble verse is a call to all sinners, infidels and others, to repent and return to God, and it informs us that God Almighty forgives all sins for whoever repents from them and turns away from them, no matter how many they are or how much they are like the foam of the sea. It is not correct to interpret this as referring to anyone other than repentance, because polytheism is not forgiven for anyone who does not repent from it. Al-Bukhari said: Ibrahim bin Musa told us, Hisham bin Yusuf told us, Ibn Jurayj told them, Ya’la said, Sa’id bin Jubair told him, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, that some people from the polytheists had killed a lot, and committed adultery a lot, so they came to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: What you say and call to is good, if only you would tell us that there is expiation for what we have done. Then the following verse was revealed: And those who do not invoke with God another deity or kill the soul which God has forbidden, except by right, and do not commit adultery and the following verse: Say, ‘O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of God.’ This is how Muslim, Abu Dawud, and al-Nasa’i narrated it from the hadith of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ya’la bin Muslim al-Makki, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both. What is meant by the first verse is the saying of God, the Most High: Except for those who repent, believe, and do righteous work verse. Imam Ahmad said: Hasan told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, Abu Qabil told us: I heard Abu Abdur-Rahman Al-Muzani say: I heard Thawban, the freed slave of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), say: I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say: “I would not like to have the world and everything in it because of this verse: ‘Say, “O My servants who have transgressed against themselves” until the end of the verse. A man said: O Messenger of God, who then associated others with God?’ The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was silent, then he said: ‘And who has associated others with God?’” three times. This is the only time Imam Ahmad narrated it. Imam Ahmad also said: Surayj ibn An-Nu’man told us: Nuh ibn Qays told us: Ash’ath ibn Jabir Al-Hadani told us: Makhul told us: Amr ibn Unbasa may God be pleased with him said: “An old man came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), leaning on a cane, and said: O Messenger of God, I have committed treachery and immorality, will I be forgiven? The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Do you not bear witness that there is no god but God? He said: Yes, and I bear witness that you are the Messenger of God. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Your treachery and immorality have been forgiven.” This is the only time Ahmad narrated it. Imam Ahmad said: Yazid bin Harun told us, Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab, on the authority of Asma bint Yazid, may God be pleased with her, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recite: Indeed, it is an unrighteous deed. And I heard him, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of God. Indeed, God forgives all sins,” and He does not mind. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful. Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi narrated it from a hadith of Thabit with it. All of these hadiths indicate that what is meant is that He forgives all of that with repentance, and a servant should not despair of God’s mercy, no matter how great and numerous his sins are, for the door of mercy and repentance is wide. God the Almighty said: Do they not know that it is God who accepts repentance from His servants? And He the Almighty said: And whoever does evil or wrongs himself but then seeks forgiveness from God will find God Forgiving and Merciful. And He the Almighty said regarding al-Munafiqun 63:“Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depths of the Fire. And never will you find for them a helper * Except for those who repent and reform.” And He the Almighty said: “Indeed, they have disbelieved who say, ‘God is the third of three.’ And there is no deity except one God. And if they do not desist from what they say, a painful punishment will surely befall those among them who disbelieve.” Then He the Almighty said: Will they not then repent to God and seek His forgiveness? And God is Forgiving and Merciful. And He the Almighty said: Indeed, those who persecuted the believing men and believing women and then did not repent. Al-Hasan al-Basri, may God have mercy on him, said: Look at this generosity and kindness. They killed His friends while He was calling them to repentance. And forgiveness and verses on this subject are very numerous. In the two Sahihs, on the authority of Abu Saeed may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him), there is the hadith of the man who killed ninety-nine people, then he regretted it and asked a worshipper from among the children of Israel if there was any chance for him to repent. He said: No. So he killed him and completed one hundred with him. Then he asked one of their scholars if there was any chance for him to repent. He said: Who will stand between you and repentance? Then he ordered him to go to a town where God would be worshipped. So he went there, but death came to him on the way, and the angels of mercy and the angels of punishment argued over him. So God, the Almighty, ordered them to measure the distance between the two lands; to whichever of them he was closer, he would be from it. They found him closer to the land to which he had migrated, so the angels of mercy took him. It was mentioned that he held his chest at the time of death and that God, the Blessed and Exalted, ordered the better town to come closer and ordered that town to move away. This is the meaning of the hadith, and we have written it in another place with its wording. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, regarding the Almighty’s saying: “Say, ‘O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of God. Indeed, God forgives all sins,’” to the end of the verse. He said: God Almighty has called to His forgiveness whoever claims that the Messiah is God, whoever claims that the Messiah is the son of God, whoever claims that Ezra is the son of God, whoever claims that God is poor, whoever claims that God’s hand is tied, and whoever claims that God is the third of three. God Almighty says to these al-Nas 114:Will they not then repent to God and seek His forgiveness? And God is Forgiving and Merciful. Then He called to repentance the one who is greater in speech than these, the one who says, I am your highest lord, and says, I have not known for you any god other than Me. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said: Whoever despairs of God’s servants of repentance after this has denied the Book of God Almighty, but the servant is not able to repent until God repents to him. Al-Tabarani narrated on the authority of Al-Sha’bi on the authority of Sunayd bin Shakl that he said: I heard Ibn Mas’ud say that the greatest verse in the Book of God is God, there is no god but He, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining. And the most comprehensive verse in The Quran with good and evil: Indeed, God commands justice and doing good. The most joyful verse in the Quran is in Surat al-Zumar 39:Say, ‘O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of God.’ The most entrusting verse in the Book of God is: And whoever fears God - He will make for him a way out * And will provide for him from where he does not expect. Masruq said to him: You have spoken the truth. Al-A’mash narrated from Abu Sa’id from Abu Al-Kanud who said: Abdullah - meaning Ibn Mas’ud may God be pleased with him passed by a storyteller who was reminding the people, so he said: O reminder, why do you make people despair of the mercy of God? Then he recited: Say, ‘O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of God.’ Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim may God have mercy on him. He mentioned hadiths that negate despair Imam Ahmad said: Surayj ibn al-Nu'man narrated to us, Abu Ubaidah Abdul-Mu'min ibn Ubaidullah narrated to us, Hasan al-Sadousi narrated to me, he said: I entered upon Anas ibn Malik may God be pleased with him and he said: I heard the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) say: "By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, if you were to sin until your sins filled the space between the heaven and the earth, and then you were to seek forgiveness from God, He would forgive you. By the One in Whose Hand is the soul of Muhammad (blessings and peace of God be upon him), if you did not sin, God would bring forth a people who would sin and then seek forgiveness from God, and He would forgive them." This is the only hadith narrated by Ahmad. Imam Ahmad said: Ishaq ibn 'Eesa narrated to us, al-Layth narrated to me, Muhammad ibn Qays Qass narrated to me, 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to me, from Abu Sarmah, from Abu Ayyub al-Ansari may God be pleased with him, that when death approached him, he said: "I had concealed something from you that I heard from the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) who said: 'Were it not that you sin, God would create a people who would sin and He would forgive them.'" This is how Imam Ahmad narrated it. Muslim included it in his Sahih, and at-Tirmidhi both narrated it on the authority of Qutaybah, from al-Layth ibn Sa'd. Muslim narrated it from another chain of narration on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi, on the authority of Abu Sarmah, who was an Ansari companion, on the authority of Abu Ayyub, may God be pleased with them both. Imam Ahmad said: Ahmad ibn Abd al-Malik al-Harrani told us, Yahya ibn Amr ibn Malik al-Bakri told us, he said: I heard my father narrating on the authority of Abu al-Jawza’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The expiation for sin is regret. And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If you did not sin, God would bring people who would sin and He would forgive them. Ahmad alone narrated it. Abdullah ibn al-Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-A’la ibn Hammad al-Qurashi told me, Dawud ibn Abd al-Rahman told us, Abu Abdullah Maslama ibn Abdullah al-Razi told us, on the authority of Abu Amr al-Bajali, on the authority of Abd al-Malik ibn Sufyan al-Thaqafi, on the authority of Abu Ja’far Muhammad ibn Ali, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah, on the authority of his father, Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God loves the tempted servant who repents. And they did not include it from this chain of narration. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Musa bin Ismail told us, Hammad told us, Thabit and Hamid told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Ubaid bin Umair, who said: Iblis, may God curse him, said: O Lord, You have expelled me from Paradise because of Adam, and I cannot do it except with Your authority. He said: Then you have authority. He said: O Lord, give me more. He said: No child will be born to him except that a child like him will be born to you. He said: O Lord, give me more. He said: Shall I make their chests dwelling places for you and shall make blood run through them? He said: O Lord, give me more. He said: Attack them with your cavalry and infantry and share with them in wealth and children and make promises to them. But Satan promises them nothing but delusion. Adam, peace be upon him, said: O Lord, You have given him authority over me, and I cannot protect myself except through You. He said: God, the Blessed and Exalted, does not give birth to a child except that You appoint someone to protect him from bad company. He said: O Lord, give me more. He said: The good deed is ten or more and the bad deed is one or I will erase it. He said: O Lord, give me more. He said: The door of repentance is open as long as the soul is in the body. He said: O Lord, give me more. He said: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of God. Indeed, God forgives. “All sins are forgiven. Indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful.” Muhammad bin Ishaq said: Nafi’ said, on the authority of Abdullah bin Umar, on the authority of Umar, may God be pleased with them both, in his hadith: “We used to say: ‘God does not accept from those who are tempted any change, nor justice, nor repentance. They knew God, then returned to disbelief because of a calamity that befell them.’ He said: “And they used to say that to themselves.” He said: “So when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to Medina, God Almighty revealed about them and about our saying and their saying to themselves: ‘O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of God. Indeed, God forgives all sins. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful. And turn to your Lord and submit to Him before the punishment comes upon you, then you will not be aided. And follow the best of what was revealed to you from your Lord before the punishment comes upon you suddenly while you do not perceive.’” Umar, may God be pleased with him, said: So I wrote it with my own hand on a piece of paper and sent it to Hisham bin Al-‘As, may God be pleased with him. He said: “Hisham said: ‘When it came to me, I began to recite it in Dhu Tuwa, ascending it and making noise, but I did not understand it until I said: O God, make me understand it.’ So I threw it down.” God the Almighty has in my heart that it was revealed about us and what we were saying to ourselves and what was said about us, so I returned to my camel and sat on it and joined the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Medina. Then God the Almighty urged His servants to hasten to repent, saying: And turn to your Lord in repentance and submit to Him etc., meaning return to God and surrender to Him before the punishment comes upon you and then you will not be helped meaning hasten to repent and do righteous deeds before the punishment comes and follow the best of what was revealed to you from your Lord which is the Noble Qur’an before the punishment comes upon you suddenly while you do not perceive meaning from where you do not know or perceive. Then God the Almighty said: lest a soul should say, ‘Oh, how I regret what I neglected in my duty to God’ meaning on the Day of Resurrection the criminal who was negligent in repentance and returning will regret it and wish that he was among the righteous, sincere, and obedient to God the Almighty. And God the Almighty said: And if I were among the mockers meaning that my work in this world was only the work of a mocker, a scofferer, not… Certain and believing, Or you say, ‘If only God had guided me, I would have been among the righteous.’ Or you say when you see the punishment, ‘If only I had another chance so I could be among the doers of good.’ That is, you would wish you could be returned to this world so you could do good deeds. Ali ibn Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, God the Almighty informed us of what the servants say before they say it and what they do before they do it. God the Almighty said: And none informs you like the All-Knowing. “Lest a soul should say, ‘Oh, how I regret what I neglected in my duty to God, and that I was among the mockers.’ Or it should say, ‘If only God had guided me, I would have been among the righteous.’ Or it should say, when it sees the punishment, ‘If only I had another chance, I would be among the doers of good.’” Imam Ahmad said: Aswad told us: Abu Bakr told us: Al-A’mash told us: Abu Salih told us: Abu Hurayrah told us: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Everyone in Hell will see his place in Paradise and say, ‘If only God had guided me.’ That will be a regret for him. He said: And every person in Paradise will see his place in Hell and say, ‘If only God had guided me.’ That will be a sign of gratitude.” An-Nasa’i narrated it from the hadith of Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash with this chain of transmission. When the people who committed crimes wished to return to this world and regretted believing in the verses of God and following His Messengers, God Almighty said: Yes, My signs came to you, but you denied them and were arrogant and were among the disbelievers. That is, O servant who regrets what you did, My signs came to you in this world and My proofs were established against you, but you denied them and were arrogant about following them, and you were among the disbelievers who denied them.

Al-A’mash narrated from Abu Sa’id from Abu Al-Kanud who said: Abdullah - meaning Ibn Mas’ud may God be pleased with him passed by a storyteller who was reminding the people, so he said: O reminder, why do you make people despair of the mercy of God? Then he recited: Say, ‘O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of God.’ Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim may God have mercy on him. He said: Attack them with your cavalry and infantry and share with them in wealth and children and make promises to them. But Satan promises them nothing but delusion. Muslim narrated it from another chain of narration on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi, on the authority of Abu Sarmah, who was an Ansari companion, on the authority of Abu Ayyub, may God be pleased with them both. And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If you did not sin, God would bring people who would sin and He would forgive them. Ahmad alone narrated it. And they did not include it from this chain of narration. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Musa bin Ismail told us, Hammad told us, Thabit and Hamid told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Ubaid bin Umair, who said: Iblis, may God curse him, said: O Lord, You have expelled me from Paradise because of Adam, and I cannot do it except with Your authority. He said: Then you have authority. He said: O Lord, give me more. He said: No child will be born to him except that a child like him will be born to you. He said: O Lord, give me more. He said: Shall I make their chests dwelling places for you and shall make blood run through them? He said: O Lord, give me more. He said: Attack them with your cavalry and infantry and share with them in wealth and children and make promises to them. But Satan promises them nothing but delusion. Adam, peace be upon him, said: O Lord, You have given him authority over me, and I cannot protect myself except through You. He said: God, the Blessed and Exalted, does not give birth to a child except that You appoint someone to protect him from bad company. He said: O Lord, give me more. He said: The good deed is ten or more and the bad deed is one or I will erase it. He said: O Lord, give me more. He said: The door of repentance is open as long as the soul is in the body. He said: O Lord, give me more. He said: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of God. Indeed, God forgives. “All sins are forgiven. Indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful.” Muhammad bin Ishaq said: Nafi’ said, on the authority of Abdullah bin Umar, on the authority of Umar, may God be pleased with them both, in his hadith: “We used to say: ‘God does not accept from those who are tempted any change, nor justice, nor repentance. They knew God, then returned to disbelief because of a calamity that befell them.’ He said: “And they used to say that to themselves.” He said: “So when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to Medina, God Almighty revealed about them and about our saying and their saying to themselves: ‘O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of God. Indeed, God forgives all sins. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful. And turn to your Lord and submit to Him before the punishment comes upon you, then you will not be aided. And follow the best of what was revealed to you from your Lord before the punishment comes upon you suddenly while you do not perceive.’” Umar, may God be pleased with him, said: So I wrote it with my own hand on a piece of paper and sent it to Hisham bin Al-‘As, may God be pleased with him. He said: “Hisham said: ‘When it came to me, I began to recite it in Dhu Tuwa, ascending it and making noise, but I did not understand it until I said: O God, make me understand it.’ So I threw it down.” God the Almighty has in my heart that it was revealed about us and what we were saying to ourselves and what was said about us, so I returned to my camel and sat on it and joined the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Medina. Then God the Almighty urged His servants to hasten to repent, saying: And turn to your Lord in repentance and submit to Him etc., meaning return to God and surrender to Him before the punishment comes upon you and then you will not be helped meaning hasten to repent and do righteous deeds before the punishment comes and follow the best of what was revealed to you from your Lord which is the Noble Qur’an before the punishment comes upon you suddenly while you do not perceive meaning from where you do not know or perceive. Then God the Almighty said: lest a soul should say, ‘Oh, how I regret what I neglected in my duty to God’ meaning on the Day of Resurrection the criminal who was negligent in repentance and returning will regret it and wish that he was among the righteous, sincere, and obedient to God the Almighty. And God the Almighty said: And if I were among the mockers meaning that my work in this world was only the work of a mocker, a scofferer, not… Certain and believing, Or you say, ‘If only God had guided me, I would have been among the righteous.’ Or you say when you see the punishment, ‘If only I had another chance so I could be among the doers of good.’ That is, you would wish you could be returned to this world so you could do good deeds. Ali ibn Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, God the Almighty informed us of what the servants say before they say it and what they do before they do it. God the Almighty said: And none informs you like the All-Knowing. “Lest a soul should say, ‘Oh, how I regret what I neglected in my duty to God, and that I was among the mockers.’ Or it should say, ‘If only God had guided me, I would have been among the righteous.’ Or it should say, when it sees the punishment, ‘If only I had another chance, I would be among the doers of good.’” Imam Ahmad said: Aswad told us: Abu Bakr told us: Al-A’mash told us: Abu Salih told us: Abu Hurayrah told us: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Everyone in Hell will see his place in Paradise and say, ‘If only God had guided me.’ That will be a regret for him. He said: And every person in Paradise will see his place in Hell and say, ‘If only God had guided me.’ That will be a sign of gratitude.” An-Nasa’i narrated it from the hadith of Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash with this chain of transmission. That is, O servant who regrets what you did, My signs came to you in this world and My proofs were established against you, but you denied them and were arrogant about following them, and you were among the disbelievers who denied them.

Indeed, God forgives all sins. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful. And turn to your Lord and submit to Him before the punishment comes upon you, then you will not be aided. And follow the best of what was revealed to you from your Lord before the punishment comes upon you suddenly while you do not perceive.’” Umar, may God be pleased with him, said: So I wrote it with my own hand on a piece of paper and sent it to Hisham bin Al-‘As, may God be pleased with him. He said: “Hisham said: ‘When it came to me, I began to recite it in Dhu Tuwa, ascending it and making noise, but I did not understand it until I said: O God, make me understand it.’ So I threw it down.” God the Almighty has in my heart that it was revealed about us and what we were saying to ourselves and what was said about us, so I returned to my camel and sat on it and joined the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Medina. Then God the Almighty urged His servants to hasten to repent, saying: And turn to your Lord in repentance and submit to Him etc., meaning return to God and surrender to Him before the punishment comes upon you and then you will not be helped meaning hasten to repent and do righteous deeds before the punishment comes and follow the best of what was revealed to you from your Lord which is the Noble Qur’an before the punishment comes upon you suddenly while you do not perceive meaning from where you do not know or perceive. Then God the Almighty said: lest a soul should say, ‘Oh, how I regret what I neglected in my duty to God’ meaning on the Day of Resurrection the criminal who was negligent in repentance and returning will regret it and wish that he was among the righteous, sincere, and obedient to God the Almighty. And God the Almighty said: And if I were among the mockers meaning that my work in this world was only the work of a mocker, a scofferer, not… Certain and believing, Or you say, ‘If only God had guided me, I would have been among the righteous.’ Or you say when you see the punishment, ‘If only I had another chance so I could be among the doers of good.’ That is, you would wish you could be returned to this world so you could do good deeds. Ali ibn Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, God the Almighty informed us of what the servants say before they say it and what they do before they do it. God the Almighty said: And none informs you like the All-Knowing. “Lest a soul should say, ‘Oh, how I regret what I neglected in my duty to God, and that I was among the mockers.’ Or it should say, ‘If only God had guided me, I would have been among the righteous.’ Or it should say, when it sees the punishment, ‘If only I had another chance, I would be among the doers of good.’” Imam Ahmad said: Aswad told us: Abu Bakr told us: Al-A’mash told us: Abu Salih told us: Abu Hurayrah told us: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Everyone in Hell will see his place in Paradise and say, ‘If only God had guided me.’ That will be a regret for him. He said: And every person in Paradise will see his place in Hell and say, ‘If only God had guided me.’ That will be a sign of gratitude.” An-Nasa’i narrated it from the hadith of Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash with this chain of transmission. When the people who committed crimes wished to return to this world and regretted believing in the verses of God and following His Messengers, God Almighty said: Yes, My signs came to you, but you denied them and were arrogant and were among the disbelievers. That is, O servant who regrets what you did, My signs came to you in this world and My proofs were established against you, but you denied them and were arrogant about following them, and you were among the disbelievers who denied them.
39:60: On the Day of Resurrection you will see those who lied about God, their faces blackened. Is there not in Hell a residence for the arrogant? And God will save those who feared God with their place of safety. No evil will touch them, nor will they grieve. God tells us about the Day of Resurrection that some faces will blacken and some will whiten. The faces of the people of division and disagreement will blacken, and the faces of the people of the Sunnah and the Community will whiten. God the Almighty said here: And on the Day of Resurrection you will see those who lied about God meaning in their claim that He had a partner and a son. Their faces will be blackened meaning because of their lies and fabrications. And God the Almighty said: Is there not in Hell a residence for the arrogant? meaning is Hell not sufficient as a prison and a place for them to be disgraced and humiliated because of their arrogance, tyranny, and refusal to submit to the truth. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Ubaidullah, the nephew of Ibn Wahb, told us: My uncle told us: Isa bin Abi Isa al-Khayyat told us: Amr bin Shuaib, from his father, from his grandfather, may God be pleased with him, said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The arrogant will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection like ants in the form of people, with everything small above them, until they enter a prison of fire in a valley called Bolus, from the fire of the Anirams, and they will be given to drink from the pus of the people of the Fire and from the mud of Khabal.” And the words of God, the Most High: And God will save those who feared God with their place of safety meaning with what preceded them of happiness and success with God. No evil will touch them meaning on the Day of Resurrection nor will they grieve meaning the greatest terror will not grieve them, rather they will be safe from every terror, removed from every evil, attaining every good.
39:62: God Almighty informs us that He is the Creator of all things, their Lord, their King, and the One who controls them, and everything is under His control, His dominion, and His guardianship. And the Almighty says: To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth. Mujahid said: The keys are keys in Persian, and so said Qatada, Ibn Zayd, and Sufyan ibn Uyaynah. Al-Suddi said: To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth, meaning the treasuries of the heavens and the earth. The meaning according to both sayings is that the reins of affairs are in His hand, blessed and exalted be He. His is the kingdom and His is the praise, and He is over all things competent. For this reason, the Almighty said: And those who disbelieve in the signs of God, meaning His proofs and evidence, those are the losers. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated here a very strange hadith, and its authenticity is questionable, but we will mention it as he mentioned it, for he said: Yazid ibn Sinan al-Basri told us in Egypt. Yahya ibn Hammad told us. Al-Aghlab ibn Tamim told us, on the authority of Mukhallad ibn Hudhayl al-Abdi, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman al-Madani, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Umar, on the authority of Uthman ibn Affan, may God be pleased with him, that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about the interpretation of the verse: To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth. He said, No one has asked me about it before you, O Uthman. He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, “Its interpretation is: There is no god but God, and God is the Greatest, and glory be to God and praise be to Him. I seek forgiveness from God, and there is no power except with God, the First and the Last, the Evident and the Immanent. In His hand is good; He gives life and causes death, and He has power over all things.” “Whoever says it, ‘O Uthman,’ ten times in the morning, will be given six things: The first will be protected from Satan and his soldiers. The second will be given a quintal of reward. The third will be raised in rank in Paradise. The fourth will be married to the houris. The fifth will be attended by twelve angels. The sixth will be given the reward of someone who recited the Qur’an, the Torah, the Gospel, and the Psalms. In addition to this, O Uthman, he will have the reward of someone who performed Hajj and had his Hajj accepted, and of someone who performed Umrah and had his Umrah accepted. If he died that day, the seal of the martyrs will be stamped on him.” Abu Ya’la al-Mawsili narrated it from the hadith of Yahya ibn Hammad, with a similar chain of transmission. It is strange and contains strong objection, and God knows best. God the Most High said: Say, ‘Is it other than God that you order me to worship, O ignorant ones?’ They mentioned in the reason for its revelation what Ibn Abi Hatim and others narrated from Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them, that the polytheists, due to their ignorance, called the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to worship their gods and worship his god along with him. Then the verse was revealed: “Say, ‘Is it other than God that you order me to worship, O ignorant ones?’ And it has already been revealed to you, and to those before you, ‘If you should associate [anything] with God, your work would surely become worthless, and you would surely be among the losers.’” This is similar to the Almighty’s statement: And if they had associated [anything] with God, all that they used to do would surely be worthless for them. And the Almighty’s statement: Rather, worship God and be among the grateful. That is, sincerely devote your worship to God alone, with no partner for Him, you and those who follow you and believe in you.

39:67: God the Most High says: And they did not appraise God with His true appraisal meaning the polytheists did not appraise God with His true appraisal when they worshipped other than Him, though He is the Great, than whom there is none greater, the Able to do all things, the Owner of all things, and everything is under His dominance and power. Mujahid said: It was revealed about the Quraysh. Al-Suddi said: They did not glorify Him with the true appraisal. Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: If they had appraised Him with the true appraisal, they would not have lied. Ali ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both: And they did not appraise God with the true appraisal They are the disbelievers who did not believe in God's power over them. Whoever believes that God has power over all things has appraised God with the true appraisal, and whoever does not believe in that has not appraised God with the true appraisal. Many hadiths have been narrated related to this noble verse, and the way in them and similar ones is the way of the salaf, which is to pass them on as they were narrated without specifying or distorting them. Al-Bukhari said: The Almighty said: And they have not appraised God with His true appraisal. Adam told us, Shaiban told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Ubaidah, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, may God be pleased with him, who said: A rabbi from the rabbis came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Muhammad, we find that God Almighty places the heavens on one finger and the earths on one finger, and the trees on one finger, and the water and the soil on one finger, and the rest of creation on one finger, and he says, I am the King. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, laughed until his molars were visible in confirmation of the rabbi’s words. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: And they have not appraised God with His true appraisal, and the earth entirely will be in His grip on the Day of Resurrection. Al-Bukhari also narrated it in a different place in his Sahih, and Imam Ahmad, Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, and al-Nasa’i in their interpretations from their Sunans, all from the hadith of Sulayman ibn Mihran al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Ubaidah, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, may God be pleased with him, in a similar manner. Imam Ahmad said: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Alqamah, on the authority of Abdullah, may God be pleased with him, who said: A man from the People of the Book came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: O Abu al-Qasim, has it reached you that God, the Most High, carries the creation on a finger, the heavens on a finger, the earths on a finger, the trees on a finger, the water and the soil on a finger? He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, laughed until his molars showed. He said: Then God, the Almighty, revealed: And they have not appraised God with true appraisal to the end of the verse. And this is how al-Bukhari, Muslim, and al-Nasa’i narrated it through various chains of transmission on the authority of al-A’mash. Imam Ahmad said: Husayn ibn Hasan al-Ashqar told us, Abu Kudayna told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Abu al-Dahha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: A Jew passed by the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was sitting and said: How do you say, O Abu al-Qasim, about the Day when God, the Almighty, the Most High, will place the heavens on this” - and he pointed with his index finger - and the earth on this and the mountains on this and the rest of creation on this” - all of that he pointed with his fingers. He said: Then God, the Almighty, revealed: And they have not appraised God with true appraisal the verse. And this is how al-Tirmidhi narrated it in the interpretation on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Darimi, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Salt Abu Ja’far, on the authority of Abu It was narrated by Yahya bin Al-Muhallab on the authority of Ata bin Al-Saib on the authority of Abu Ad-Dhaha Muslim bin Subaih, and he said: It is good, authentic, and strange. We do not know it except from this source. Then Al-Bukhari said: Saeed bin Ufair told us, Al-Layth told us, Abd Al-Rahman bin Khalid bin Musafir told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Abu Salamah bin Abd Al-Rahman, that Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, say: “God, the Most High, will seize the earth and fold the heavens with His right hand, then He will say: I am the King. Where are the kings of the earth?” He is the only one who narrated it from this source, and Muslim narrated it from another source. Al-Bukhari said in another place: Muqaddam bin Muhammad told us, my uncle Al-Qasim bin Yahya told us, on the authority of Ubaidullah, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, may God be pleased with them both, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: On the Day of Resurrection, God, the Blessed and Exalted, will grasp the earths on a finger and the heavens will be in His right hand, then He will say, ‘I am the King.’ He also singled out this chain of transmission and it was longer. He said: Affan told us, Hammad bin Salamah told us, Ishaq bin Abdullah bin Abi Talhah told us, on the authority of Ubaidullah bin Muqsim, on the authority of Ibn Umar, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited this verse one day on the pulpit: “And they have not appraised God with His true appraisal. And the earth entirely will be in His grip on the Day of Resurrection and the heavens will be rolled up in His right hand. Glory be to Him, and He is far above what they associate with Him.” And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was saying like this with his hand, moving it forward and backward: “The Lord glorifies Himself: I am the Compeller, I am the Proud, I am the King, I am the Mighty, I am the Generous.” So the pulpit shook with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, until we thought it would collapse with him. Muslim, Al-Nasa’i, and Ibn Majah from the hadith of Abdul Aziz bin Abi Hazim, and Muslim and Yaqoub bin Abdul Rahman added, both of them on the authority of Abi Hazim, on the authority of Ubaidullah bin Muqsim, on the authority of Ibn Umar, may God be pleased with them both, with a similar wording. Muslim’s wording on the authority of Ubaidullah bin Muqsim in this hadith is that he looked at Abdullah bin Umar, may God be pleased with them both, and how he narrated the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: God, the Blessed and Exalted, will take His heavens and His earth in His hand and say, I am the King, and He clenched His fingers and spread them out, I am the King, until I saw the pulpit moving from the bottom part of it until I thought, “Is it falling with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace?” Al-Bazzar said: Sulayman bin Saif told us, Abu Ali al-Hanafi told us, Ibad al-Munqari told us, Muhammad bin al-Munkadir told us, he said: Abdullah bin Umar, may God be pleased with them both, told us that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited this verse on the pulpit: “And they have not appraised God with true appraisal. And the earth entirely will be in His grip on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens will be rolled up in His right hand. Glory be to Him, and He is exalted above what they associate with Him.” Then the pulpit said thus, and it came and went three times, and God knows best. Imam al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani narrated it on the authority of Ubayd bin Umair on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, may God be pleased with them both, and he said: It is authentic. Al-Tabarani said in Al-Mu’jam Al-Kabir: Abd Al-Rahman bin Mu’awiyah Al-Utbi told us, Hayyan bin Nafi’ told us, on the authority of Sakhr bin Juwayriyah, on the authority of Saeed bin Salem Al-Qaddah, on the authority of Muammar bin Al-Hasan, on the authority of Bakr bin Khunais, on the authority of Abu Shaiba, on the authority of Abd Al-Malik bin Umair, on the authority of Jarir, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to a group of his companions, may God be pleased with them: “I am going to recite to you verses from the end of Surat Az-Zumar. Whoever among you weeps, Paradise will be guaranteed for him.” So he, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited them from and they did not appraise God with His true appraisal to the end of the surah. Some of us wept and some of us did not. Those who did not weep said: O Messenger of God, we did our best to weep but we did not. So he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I will recite them to you, so whoever does not weep, let him pretend to be. This is a very strange hadith, and even stranger than it is what he also narrated in Al-Mu’jam Al-Kabir: Hashim bin Zaid told us, Muhammad bin Ismail bin Ayyash told us, my father told me, Damdam bin Zar’ah told me, on the authority of Shuraih bin Ubaid, on the authority of Abu Malik Al-Ash’ari, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God’s Messenger (may peace and blessings be upon him) said: “God the Most High says, ‘There are three things during which I am absent from My servants, if a man were to see them, he would never do anything wrong: If I were to remove My covering and see Me until he is certain and knows how I act with My creation when I come to them and I grasp the heavens with My hand, then I grasp the earths, then I say, ‘I am the King. Who has a kingdom other than Me?’ Then I will show them Paradise and all that I have prepared for them therein of every good, so that they may be certain of it. And I will show them Hell and all that I have prepared for them therein of every evil, so that they may be certain of it. But I intentionally concealed that from them so that I may know how they will act, and I have made it clear to them.” This is a similar chain of transmission, and it is a version with which many hadiths are narrated, and God knows best.
39:68: The Blessed and Exalted says, informing about the horror of the Day of Resurrection and the great signs and tremendous earthquakes that will occur in it. The Almighty says: And the Trumpet will be blown, and all who are in the heavens and the earth will fall dead except whom God wills. This is the second blast, and it is the blast of the stunner, by which the living among the people of the heavens and the earth will die except whom God wills, as was stated explicitly and explained in the famous hadith of the Trumpet. Then the souls of those who remain will be taken until the last to die is the Angel of Death, and the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining, who was first and is the Remaining, will be alone in perpetuity and survival. He will say three times, To God, the One, the Compeller. I am the One who was alone and I have conquered all things and decreed the annihilation of all things. Then He will revive the first to revive, Israfil, and command him to blow the Trumpet again, and this is the third blast, the blast of resurrection. God the Almighty said: Then He will blow into it again, and at once they will be standing, looking on. That is, alive after they had been bones and dust that had become… The living are looking at the horrors of the Day of Resurrection, as God the Almighty said: “It will be only a single shout. At once they will be awake.” And God the Almighty said: The Day He will call you, and you will respond with praise to Him and you will think that you had remained only a little. And He the Almighty said: “And among His signs is that the heaven and the earth stand by His command. Then when He calls you with a single call from the earth, at once you will come forth.” Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja’far told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of al-Nu’man ibn Salim, who said: I heard Ya’qub ibn ‘Asim ibn ‘Urwah ibn Mas’ud say: I heard a man say to ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Amr may God be pleased with them both: You say that the Hour will come to an end at such and such a time. He said: “I intended not to tell you anything. I only said: ‘You will see in a little while a tremendous matter.’” Then ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Amr may God be pleased with them both said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The Antichrist will emerge among my nation and will remain among them for forty – I do not know if it will be forty days, forty months, forty years, or forty nights. Then God, the Most High, will send Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him, looking like Urwah ibn Mas`ud al-Thaqafi. He will appear and God, the Most High, will destroy him. Then the people will remain after him for seven years, with no enmity between two people. Then God, the Most High, will send a cold wind from the direction of Ash-Sham, and no one will remain in whose heart there is an atom’s weight of faith except that it will seize him, so that if one of them were to be in the middle of a mountain, it would enter upon him.” He said: I heard it from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. “And the worst of people will remain in the lightness of birds and dreams of wild beasts. They will not recognize what is right nor denounce what is wrong.” He said: “Then Satan will appear to them and say: ‘Will you not respond?’ He will command them to worship idols, and they will worship them. In that, they will have their provisions and good lives. Then the Trumpet will be blown, and no one will hear it except that he will listen to it. The first to hear it will be a man who will fill his cistern and be struck dead. Then no one will remain except that he will be struck dead. Then God, the Most High, will send or send down…” God, the Almighty, will send rain like dew - or dew, Nu'man was unsure - and the bodies of people will grow from it. Then He will blow into it again, and at once they will be standing, looking on. Then it will be said, O people, come to your Lord. Stop them, for indeed, they will be questioned. Then it will be said, Bring forth the people of the Fire. He will be asked, How many? It will be said, "Out of every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine. On that Day the children will be raised up as white hairs, and on that Day the shin will be uncovered." Muslim alone transmitted it in his Sahih. Hadith of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him Al-Bukhari said: Umar ibn Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Al-A’mash said: I heard Abu Salih say: I heard Abu Hurairah may God be pleased with him narrating on the authority of the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) who said: Between the two blasts will be forty. They said: O Abu Hurairah, forty days? He may God be pleased with him said: I refuse. They said: Forty years? He said: I refuse. They said: Forty months? He said: I refuse. And everything of man will decay except his coccyx, on which creation is reconstructed. Abu Ya'la said: Yahya bin Ma'in told us, Abu Al-Yaman told us, Ismail bin Ayyash told us, on the authority of Umar bin Muhammad, on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him), who said: "I asked Gabriel (peace be upon him) about this verse, 'And the Trumpet will be blown, and all who are in the heavens and the earth will fall dead except whom God wills.' Who are those whom God wills not to fall dead? He said, 'They are the martyrs, wearing their swords around His Throne, and the angels will meet them on the Day of Resurrection to the place of assembly, riding camels of rubies, their steps softer than silk, as far as the sight of men can reach. They will walk in Paradise and say, when the excursion is long, 'Come with us to our Lord so that we may see how He judges between His creation.' He laughs at them, 'O my God, and if He laughs at a servant in a place, then there is no account for him.'" All of its men are trustworthy except for the sheikh of Ismail bin Ayyash, for he is not well-known, and God, the Most High, the Most Great, knows best. And the words of God, the Most High: And the earth will shine with the light of its Lord, meaning it will be illuminated on the Day of Resurrection when the Truth, the Most High, is revealed to creation to decide the judgment. And the Book will be placed, Qatadah said, The Book of deeds, “And the prophets will be brought,” Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said, They will bear witness against the nations that they delivered God’s messages to them, “And the witnesses,” meaning the angelic witnesses who preserve the deeds of the servants, both good and evil. And it will be judged between them with truth, meaning with justice, and they will not be wronged. God, the Most High, said: “And We will set up the just scales for the Day of Resurrection, so that no soul will be wronged at all. And if there is [anything] the weight of a mustard seed, We will bring it forth. And sufficient are We as accountants.” And God, the Most High, said: “Indeed, God does not wrong [anyone] by the weight of an atom. And if there is a good deed, He multiplies it and gives from Himself a great reward.” For this reason, God, the Most High, said: And every soul will be fully compensated for what it has done, meaning of good and evil, And He is most knowing of what they do.

39:71: God the Almighty tells us about the state of the wretched disbelievers, how they will be driven to Hellfire. They will be driven violently, with rebuke, threat and warning, as God the Almighty said: The Day they will be summoned to the Fire of Hell, a summons. That is, they will be pushed into it forcefully, and they will be thirsty and thirsty, as God the Almighty said in another verse: The Day We will gather the righteous to the Most Merciful as a delegation, and drive the criminals to Hellfire in droves. In that state, they will be deaf, dumb and blind, some of them walking on their faces. “And We will gather them on the Day of Resurrection on their faces, blind, dumb and deaf. Their refuge is Hell. Whenever it subsides, We will increase their Blaze.” And God the Almighty said: Until, when they reach it, its gates are opened. That is, as soon as they arrive at it, its gates are quickly opened to hasten their punishment. Then its keepers from among the guards, who are harsh in character and strong in strength, will say to them, in a manner of rebuke, reprimand and torment, Did there not come to you messengers from among you? That is, from your kind, you are able to address them and learn from them. They recite to you the verses of your Lord, that is, they establish before you arguments and proofs for the truth of what they have called you to. And they warn you of the meeting of this Day of yours, that is, they warn you of the evil of this Day. The disbelievers will say to them, Yes, that is, they have come to us and warned us and established arguments and proofs against us. But the word of punishment has come into effect upon the disbelievers, that is, but we denied them and disobeyed them because of the misery that we had previously deserved when we turned from the truth to falsehood, as God Almighty said, informing us about them in another verse: “Whenever a group is thrown into it, its keepers will ask them, ‘Did there not come to you a warner?’ They will say, ‘Yes, a warner did come to us, but we denied it and said, ‘God has not sent down anything. You are not except in great error.’ And they will say, ‘If only we had listened or used reason, we would not have been among the companions of the Blaze.’” That is, they will turn back on themselves with blame and remorse. “So they will acknowledge their sin. So away with the companions of the Blaze,” that is, far away from them and loss. And His, the Blessed and Most High, saying here, It will be said, ‘Enter the gates of Hell to abide therein eternally.’ That is, everyone who sees them and knows their condition will testify against them that they deserve the punishment. For this reason, He did not attribute this statement to a specific speaker, but rather made it general to indicate that the universe is a witness against them that they deserve what they are in, according to the judgment of the All-Knowing, Just One. For this reason, the Most High, the Most Great, said, It will be said, ‘Enter the gates of Hell to abide therein eternally.’ That is, remaining in it, with no exit from it for you and no departure from it. So evil is the residence of the arrogant. That is, so evil is the destination and evil is the resting place for you because of your arrogance in this world and your refusal to follow the truth. It is what brought you to what you are in. So evil is the condition and evil is the outcome.
