That is, as soon as they arrive at it, its gates are quickly opened to hasten their punishment. Then its keepers from among the guards, who are harsh in character and strong in strength, will say to them, in a manner of rebuke, reprimand and torment, Did there not come to you messengers from among you? That is, from your kind, you are able to address them and learn from them. They recite to you the verses of your Lord, that is, they establish before you arguments and proofs for the truth of what they have called you to. And they warn you of the meeting of this Day of yours, that is, they warn you of the evil of this Day. The disbelievers will say to them, Yes, that is, they have come to us and warned us and established arguments and proofs against us. But the word of punishment has come into effect upon the disbelievers, that is, but we denied them and disobeyed them because of the misery that we had previously deserved when we turned from the truth to falsehood, as God Almighty said, informing us about them in another verse: “Whenever a group is thrown into it, its keepers will ask them, ‘Did there not come to you a warner?’ They will say, ‘Yes, a warner did come to us, but we denied it and said, ‘God has not sent down anything. You are not except in great error.’ And they will say, ‘If only we had listened or used reason, we would not have been among the companions of the Blaze.’” That is, they will turn back on themselves with blame and remorse. “So they will acknowledge their sin. So away with the companions of the Blaze,” that is, far away from them and loss. And His, the Blessed and Most High, saying here, It will be said, ‘Enter the gates of Hell to abide therein eternally.’ That is, everyone who sees them and knows their condition will testify against them that they deserve the punishment. For this reason, He did not attribute this statement to a specific speaker, but rather made it general to indicate that the universe is a witness against them that they deserve what they are in, according to the judgment of the All-Knowing, Just One. For this reason, the Most High, the Most Great, said, It will be said, ‘Enter the gates of Hell to abide therein eternally.’ That is, remaining in it, with no exit from it for you and no departure from it. So evil is the residence of the arrogant. That is, so evil is the destination and evil is the resting place for you because of your arrogance in this world and your refusal to follow the truth. It is what brought you to what you are in. So evil is the condition and evil is the outcome.
39:73: This is report about the state of the happy believers when they are driven on the camels as a delegation to Paradise in groups, i.e. group after group: the close ones, then the righteous, then those who come after them, then those who come after them, each group with those who are suitable for them: the prophets and the truthful with their likes, the martyrs with their peers, and the scholars with their peers, and each group with its own group, each group is suitable for the other. Until when they reach it, i.e. when they reach the gates of Paradise after crossing the Sirat, they are stopped on a bridge between Paradise and Hell, and retribution is made for them for the injustices that were between them in this world, until when they are refined and purified, permission is given to them to enter Paradise. It was mentioned in the hadith of the trumpets that when the believers reach the gates of Paradise, they consult about who will ask permission for them to enter, so they go to Adam, then Noah, then Abraham, then Moses, then Jesus, then Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and all of them, as they did in the gathering places when they interceded with God Almighty to come to decide the judgment, so that the honor of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, over all of humanity would be made clear in All citizens have been proven in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Anas, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I am the first intercessor in Paradise. And in a wording by Muslim: And I am the first to knock on the door of Paradise. Imam Ahmad said: Hashim told us, Sulayman told us, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I will come to the gate of Paradise on the Day of Resurrection and ask to be admitted. The gatekeeper will say, ‘Who are you?’ I will say, ‘Muhammad.’ He said, ‘Then he will say, ‘Because of you, I was commanded not to open for anyone before you.’” Muslim narrated it on the authority of Amr ibn Muhammad al-Naqid and Zuhayr ibn Harb, both of them on the authority of Abu al-Nadr Hashim ibn al-Qasim, on the authority of Sulayman, who is ibn al-Mughirah al-Qaysi, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas, may God be pleased with him, with this chain of transmission. Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Hammam ibn Munabbih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “The first group to enter Paradise will have the form of the moon on a full moon night. They will not spit therein, nor blow their noses therein, nor defecate therein. Their utensils and combs will be of gold and silver, their incense burners will be of aloe vera, and their sweat will be of musk. Each one of them will have two wives, the marrow of whose shins will be visible through the flesh because of their beauty. There will be no difference between them, nor any hatred between them. Their hearts will be one. They glorify God morning and evening.” Al-Bukhari narrated it on the authority of Muhammad ibn Muqatil, on the authority of Ibn al-Mubarak. Muslim narrated it on the authority of Muhammad ibn Rafi’, on the authority of Abd al-Razzaq, both of them on the authority of Muammar, with a similar chain of transmission. Abu al-Zinad narrated it likewise on the authority of al-A’raj, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Al-Hafiz Abu Ya`la said: Abu Khaithama told us, Jarir told us, on the authority of `Ammarah ibn al-Qa`qa`, on the authority of Abu Zur`ah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The first group to enter Paradise will be like the moon on a full moon night. Those who follow them will be like the brightest shining star in the sky. They will not urinate, defecate, spit, or blow their noses. Their combs will be gold and silver, their sweat will be musk, their incense burners will be aloe vera, and their wives will be the wide-eyed houris. Their character will be like the character of one man, in the image of their father Adam, sixty cubits high in the sky.” And they both included it in their collections from the hadith of Jarir. Al-Zuhri said, on the authority of Sa`id, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “A group of seventy thousand from my nation will enter Paradise. Their faces will shine like the brightness of the moon on a full moon night.” `Ukasha ibn Mihsan stood up and said: O Messenger of God, supplicate to God to make me one of them. He said: O God, make him one of them. Then a man from the Ansar stood up and said: O Messenger of God, supplicate to God Almighty to make me one of them. He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: He has preceded you. It was narrated by ‘Ukasha. They both included this hadith - about the seventy thousand who will enter Paradise without being brought to account - by al-Bukhari and Muslim on the authority of Ibn ‘Abbas may God be pleased with them both, Jabir ibn ‘Abdullah, ‘Imran ibn Husayn, Ibn Mas‘ud, Rifa’ah ibn ‘Arabah al-Juhani, and Umm Qays bint Muhsin may God be pleased with them both. They also included it on the authority of Abu Hazim on the authority of Sahl ibn Sa’d may God be pleased with him that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “Seventy thousand or seven hundred thousand of my nation will enter Paradise, some of them taking others into account, until the first and the last of them will enter Paradise, their faces like the moon on a full moon night.” Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah said: Ismail bin Ayyash told us on the authority of Muhammad bin Ziyad who said: I heard Abu Umamah al-Bahili may God be pleased with him say: I heard the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) say: “My Lord, the Almighty, promised me that seventy thousand of my nation will enter Paradise, with each thousand seventy thousand who will not be brought to account or punished, and three handfuls of the handfuls of my Lord, the Almighty.” And this is how al-Walid bin Muslim narrated it on the authority of Safwan bin Amr on the authority of Salim bin Amir on the authority of Abu al-Yaman Amir bin Abdullah bin Luhay on the authority of Abu Umamah. And al-Tabarani narrated it on the authority of Utbah bin Abd al-Salami: Then with each thousand seventy thousand. And something similar was narrated on the authority of Thawban and Abu Sa’id al-Anmari, and it has corroborating evidence from many sources. And the Almighty’s saying: “Until, when they come to it and its gates are opened and its keepers say to them, ‘Peace be upon you, you are well, so enter it to abide therein eternally.’” The answer is not mentioned here, but rather it is understood as: “Until, when they come to it and these matters of the gates being opened for them are an honor and awe, and the guardian angels receive them with good tidings, peace, and praise, not as the guards receive the unbelievers with reproach and rebuke.” So it is understood that if this is the case, they will be happy, content, pleased, and rejoice to the extent that they will have bliss in it. And if the answer is omitted here, the mind will go astray in every direction regarding hope and expectation. And whoever claims that the and in the Almighty’s saying: and its gates are opened is the and of eight, and uses it as evidence that the gates of Paradise are eight, has gone too far and is drowning in emptiness. Rather, the fact that the gates of Paradise are eight is derived from the authentic hadiths. Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever spends two pairs of his wealth in the way of God Almighty will be called from the gates of Paradise, and Paradise has gates. Whoever is among the people of prayer will be called from the gate of prayer. Whoever is among the people of charity will be called from the gate of charity. Whoever is among the people of jihad will be called from the gate of jihad. Whoever is among the people of fasting will be called from the gate of Rayyan.” Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, said: O Messenger of God, if someone is in need, he will be called from whichever of them he will be called. Will anyone be called from all of them, O Messenger of God? He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Yes, and I hope that you will be one of them. Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Al-Zuhri in a similar manner. In both of them, it is narrated from the hadith of Abu Hazim Salamah ibn Dinar from Sahl ibn Sa’d may God be pleased with him that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Indeed, Paradise has eight gates, one of which is called Ar-Rayyan. None shall enter it except those who fast.” In Sahih Muslim, it is narrated from Umar ibn Al-Khattab may God be pleased with him that he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “There is none among you who performs ablution and completes it completely, then says: ‘I bear witness that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger,’ except that the eight gates of Paradise will be opened for him, and he may enter through whichever one he wishes.” Al-Hasan ibn Arafa said: Ismail ibn Ayyash narrated to us from Abdullah ibn Abd Al-Rahman ibn Abi Husayn from Shahr ibn Hawshab from Mu’adh may God be pleased with him that he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “The key to Paradise is: ‘There is no god but God.’” Mentioning the vastness of the gates of Paradise - we ask God from His great grace to make us among its people In the two Sahihs, on the authority of Abu Zur’ah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, in the long hadith of intercession, “God Almighty will say, ‘O Muhammad, admit those of your nation who will not be held accountable through the right gate, and they will be partners with the people in the other gates. By the One in Whose Hand is the soul of Muhammad, the distance between the two leaflets of Paradise is like the distance between the two doorposts of the gate, like the distance between Mecca and Hajar – or Hajar and Mecca – and in another narration – Mecca and Busra.’” In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Utbah ibn Ghazwan, he delivered a sermon in which he said, It has been mentioned to us that the distance between the two leaflets of Paradise is a journey of forty years, and a day will come when it will be very crowded. In Al-Musnad, on the authority of Hakim ibn Mu’awiyah, on the authority of his father, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar. Abd ibn Hamid said, “Al-Hasan ibn Musa told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, Darraj told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Haytham, on the authority of Abu Sa’id, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said, ‘The distance between the two leaflets of Paradise is a journey of forty years.’” And the saying of God, the Most High: “And its keepers will say to them, ‘Peace be upon you. You have been good.’” That is, your deeds and words have been good, your efforts have been good, and your reward has been good, just as the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was commanded to call out among the Muslims during some of the battles, Indeed, Paradise will not be entered by anyone except a Muslim soul - and in another narration - a believer. And His saying, So enter it to abide therein forever, that is, remaining therein forever, not seeking to leave it. And they will say, ‘Praise be to God, who has fulfilled His promise to us.’ That is, the believers will say when they see in Paradise that abundant reward, bounty, lasting bliss, and great kingdom, they will say at that time, Praise be to God, who has fulfilled His promise to us, that is, who promised us on the tongues of His noble messengers, just as they called out in this world, “Our Lord, and give us what You promised us through Your messengers and do not disgrace us on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, You do not fail to fulfill Your promise.” “And they will say, ‘Praise be to God, who has guided us to this. We would not have been guided had God not guided us. The messengers of our Lord have brought the truth.’” “And they will say, ‘Praise be to God, who has removed from us sorrow. Indeed, our Lord…’” Indeed, He is Forgiving and Appreciative. * Who has settled us in the home of permanence out of His bounty. No toil will touch us therein, nor will weariness touch us therein. And His statement, “And We have given inheritance to the earth, that we may settle in Paradise wherever we will. How excellent is the reward of the workers.” Abu Al-Aaliyah, Abu Salih, Qatadah, As-Suddi, and Ibn Zayd said, meaning the land of Paradise. So this verse is like the statement of God, the Most High, And We had already written in the Psalms, after the remembrance, ‘The earth will be inherited by My righteous servants.’ For this reason they said, We may settle in Paradise wherever we will, meaning wherever we will we may settle. How excellent is our reward for our work. In the two Sahihs, from the hadith of Az-Zuhri, from Anas, may God be pleased with him, in the story of the Ascension, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, I was brought into Paradise, and there were wings of pearls and its soil was musk. Abdul Rahman bin Hamid said: Ruh bin Ubadah told us, Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Al-Jariry, on the authority of Abu Nadrah, on the authority of Abu Saeed, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked Ibn Sayyad about the soil of Paradise, and he said: The pearls of Mecca are white, pure musk. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: He is speaking the truth. Muslim narrated it in the same way from the hadith of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Nadrah, on the authority of Abu Saeed, may God be pleased with him, with it. Muslim also narrated it on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah, on the authority of Abu Usamah, on the authority of Al-Jariry, on the authority of Abu Nadrah, on the authority of Abu Saeed, may God be pleased with him, who said: Ibn Sayyad asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the soil of Paradise, and he said: The pearls of Mecca are white, pure musk. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abu Ghassan Malik bin Ismail told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Asim bin Damrah, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, regarding the words of God Almighty: And those who feared their Lord will be driven to Paradise in groups, he said: They were driven until they reached one of the gates of Paradise and found near it a tree from beneath whose trunk two springs were emerging. They went to one of them and purified themselves from it, and the freshness of bliss flowed over them, and their skins never changed after that, and their hair never became disheveled after that, as if they had been anointed with oil. Then they went to the other, as if they had been commanded to do so, and they drank from it, and it removed whatever harm or impurity was in their bellies. The angels met them at the gates of Paradise, “Peace be upon you. You have become pure, so enter it to abide therein.” And each of the boys met their companion, circling around him as boys do to boiling water. He came from absence, Be of good cheer, for God has prepared for you such and such an honor, and God has prepared for you such and such an honor. He said: And one of his boys went to his wives from the houris and said: This is so-and-so. In His name in this world, they say, Did you see him? He says, Yes. Joy overwhelms them until they go out to the threshold of the door. He says, So he comes and sees cushions lined up, cups placed, and carpets spread out. He says, “Then he looks at the foundation of his building and sees that it is built on pearls of red, green, yellow, white, and every other color. Then he raises his eyes to its ceiling. Had it not been that God Almighty had decreed it for him, he would have been pained that his sight would be lost. It is like lightning.” Then he looks at his wives from the houris, then he reclines on one of his couches and says, “Praise be to God who has guided us to this. We would not have been guided had God not guided us.” Then he said: My father told us, Abu Ghassan Malik bin Ismail Al-Nahdi told us, Maslama bin Ja’far Al-Bajali told us, he said: I heard Abu Mu’adh Al-Basri say that Ali, may God be pleased with him, was one day with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, when they emerge from their graves, they will be met by - or given - she-camels with wings, and on them are saddles of gold, the straps of their sandals, and a light will shine with every step as far as the eye can see. Then they will come to a tree from whose root two springs will spring forth. They will drink from one of them, and it will wash away whatever filth is in their bellies, and they will wash themselves from the other, and their skin and hair will never be disheveled after that, and the freshness of bliss will flow over them. Then they will come to - or they will come to - the gate of Paradise, and there will be a ring of red ruby on gold plates. They will strike the ring on the plate, and a ringing will be heard from above, and every houri will be informed that her husband has arrived, so her guardian will be sent, and it will be opened for him. When she sees him, she will fall down before him.” Maslama said: “I think he said: Prostrating - He says: Raise your head, for I am your guardian and I have been entrusted with your affair. So he follows him and tracks his footsteps. Then the hasty houri will be deceived and come out from the tents of pearls and rubies until she embraces him and says: You are my love and I am your love. I am the immortal one who does not die. I am the gentle one who does not suffer. I am the satisfied one who does not get angry. I am the resident one who does not move. So he enters a house from its foundation to its roof, a distance of one hundred thousand cubits. Its construction is made of pearl stones, with paths of yellow, green, and red in which there is no path that can rival its companion. In the house are seventy beds. On each bed are seventy mattresses. On each mattress are seventy wives. On each wife are seventy garments. The marrow of her leg can be seen from inside the garments. He completes intercourse with her in the space of one of your nights. Rivers flow from beneath them. “Rivers of water unpolluted” - he said: clear, with no turbidity in it - and rivers of milk whose taste never changes - he said: it did not come out of the udders of cattle - and rivers of wine delicious to those who drink - he said: it was not squeezed out by men with their feet. And rivers of purified honey - he said it did not come out of the bellies of bees, he gathers the fruits, if he wishes standing, if he wishes sitting, or if he wishes reclining - then he recited And its shades are drawn low for them, and its fruits are made accessible to them so he desires food and a white bird comes to him, he said or he said green, he said it raises its wings and he eats from its sides whichever color he wishes, then it flies and goes and the angel enters and says: Peace be upon you. This is Paradise, which you have inherited for what you used to do. And if a hair from the hair of the houri fell to the ground, the sun would shine with it black in light. This is a strange hadith and it seems to be mursal, and God knows best.

Rather, the fact that the gates of Paradise are eight is derived from the authentic hadiths. Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever spends two pairs of his wealth in the way of God Almighty will be called from the gates of Paradise, and Paradise has gates. Whoever is among the people of prayer will be called from the gate of prayer. Whoever is among the people of charity will be called from the gate of charity. Whoever is among the people of jihad will be called from the gate of jihad. Whoever is among the people of fasting will be called from the gate of Rayyan.” Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, said: O Messenger of God, if someone is in need, he will be called from whichever of them he will be called. Will anyone be called from all of them, O Messenger of God? He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Yes, and I hope that you will be one of them. Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Al-Zuhri in a similar manner. In both of them, it is narrated from the hadith of Abu Hazim Salamah ibn Dinar from Sahl ibn Sa’d may God be pleased with him that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Indeed, Paradise has eight gates, one of which is called Ar-Rayyan. None shall enter it except those who fast.” In Sahih Muslim, it is narrated from Umar ibn Al-Khattab may God be pleased with him that he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “There is none among you who performs ablution and completes it completely, then says: ‘I bear witness that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger,’ except that the eight gates of Paradise will be opened for him, and he may enter through whichever one he wishes.” Al-Hasan ibn Arafa said: Ismail ibn Ayyash narrated to us from Abdullah ibn Abd Al-Rahman ibn Abi Husayn from Shahr ibn Hawshab from Mu’adh may God be pleased with him that he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “The key to Paradise is: ‘There is no god but God.’” Mentioning the vastness of the gates of Paradise - we ask God from His great grace to make us among its people In the two Sahihs, on the authority of Abu Zur’ah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, in the long hadith of intercession, “God Almighty will say, ‘O Muhammad, admit those of your nation who will not be held accountable through the right gate, and they will be partners with the people in the other gates. By the One in Whose Hand is the soul of Muhammad, the distance between the two leaflets of Paradise is like the distance between the two doorposts of the gate, like the distance between Mecca and Hajar – or Hajar and Mecca – and in another narration – Mecca and Busra.’” In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Utbah ibn Ghazwan, he delivered a sermon in which he said, It has been mentioned to us that the distance between the two leaflets of Paradise is a journey of forty years, and a day will come when it will be very crowded. In Al-Musnad, on the authority of Hakim ibn Mu’awiyah, on the authority of his father, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar. Abd ibn Hamid said, “Al-Hasan ibn Musa told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, Darraj told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Haytham, on the authority of Abu Sa’id, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said, ‘The distance between the two leaflets of Paradise is a journey of forty years.’” And the saying of God, the Most High: “And its keepers will say to them, ‘Peace be upon you. You have been good.’” That is, your deeds and words have been good, your efforts have been good, and your reward has been good, just as the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was commanded to call out among the Muslims during some of the battles, Indeed, Paradise will not be entered by anyone except a Muslim soul - and in another narration - a believer. And His saying, So enter it to abide therein forever, that is, remaining therein forever, not seeking to leave it. And they will say, ‘Praise be to God, who has fulfilled His promise to us.’ That is, the believers will say when they see in Paradise that abundant reward, bounty, lasting bliss, and great kingdom, they will say at that time, Praise be to God, who has fulfilled His promise to us, that is, who promised us on the tongues of His noble messengers, just as they called out in this world, “Our Lord, and give us what You promised us through Your messengers and do not disgrace us on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, You do not fail to fulfill Your promise.” “And they will say, ‘Praise be to God, who has guided us to this. We would not have been guided had God not guided us. The messengers of our Lord have brought the truth.’” “And they will say, ‘Praise be to God, who has removed from us sorrow. Indeed, our Lord…’” Indeed, He is Forgiving and Appreciative. * Who has settled us in the home of permanence out of His bounty. No toil will touch us therein, nor will weariness touch us therein. And His statement, “And We have given inheritance to the earth, that we may settle in Paradise wherever we will. How excellent is the reward of the workers.” Abu Al-Aaliyah, Abu Salih, Qatadah, As-Suddi, and Ibn Zayd said, meaning the land of Paradise. So this verse is like the statement of God, the Most High, And We had already written in the Psalms, after the remembrance, ‘The earth will be inherited by My righteous servants.’ For this reason they said, We may settle in Paradise wherever we will, meaning wherever we will we may settle. How excellent is our reward for our work. In the two Sahihs, from the hadith of Az-Zuhri, from Anas, may God be pleased with him, in the story of the Ascension, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, I was brought into Paradise, and there were wings of pearls and its soil was musk. Abdul Rahman bin Hamid said: Ruh bin Ubadah told us, Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Al-Jariry, on the authority of Abu Nadrah, on the authority of Abu Saeed, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked Ibn Sayyad about the soil of Paradise, and he said: The pearls of Mecca are white, pure musk. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: He is speaking the truth. Muslim narrated it in the same way from the hadith of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Nadrah, on the authority of Abu Saeed, may God be pleased with him, with it. Muslim also narrated it on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah, on the authority of Abu Usamah, on the authority of Al-Jariry, on the authority of Abu Nadrah, on the authority of Abu Saeed, may God be pleased with him, who said: Ibn Sayyad asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the soil of Paradise, and he said: The pearls of Mecca are white, pure musk. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abu Ghassan Malik bin Ismail told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Asim bin Damrah, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, regarding the words of God Almighty: And those who feared their Lord will be driven to Paradise in groups, he said: They were driven until they reached one of the gates of Paradise and found near it a tree from beneath whose trunk two springs were emerging. They went to one of them and purified themselves from it, and the freshness of bliss flowed over them, and their skins never changed after that, and their hair never became disheveled after that, as if they had been anointed with oil. Then they went to the other, as if they had been commanded to do so, and they drank from it, and it removed whatever harm or impurity was in their bellies. The angels met them at the gates of Paradise, “Peace be upon you. You have become pure, so enter it to abide therein.” And each of the boys met their companion, circling around him as boys do to boiling water. He came from absence, Be of good cheer, for God has prepared for you such and such an honor, and God has prepared for you such and such an honor. He said: And one of his boys went to his wives from the houris and said: This is so-and-so. In His name in this world, they say, Did you see him? He says, Yes. Joy overwhelms them until they go out to the threshold of the door. He says, So he comes and sees cushions lined up, cups placed, and carpets spread out. He says, “Then he looks at the foundation of his building and sees that it is built on pearls of red, green, yellow, white, and every other color. Then he raises his eyes to its ceiling. Had it not been that God Almighty had decreed it for him, he would have been pained that his sight would be lost. It is like lightning.” Then he looks at his wives from the houris, then he reclines on one of his couches and says, “Praise be to God who has guided us to this. We would not have been guided had God not guided us.” Then he said: My father told us, Abu Ghassan Malik bin Ismail Al-Nahdi told us, Maslama bin Ja’far Al-Bajali told us, he said: I heard Abu Mu’adh Al-Basri say that Ali, may God be pleased with him, was one day with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, when they emerge from their graves, they will be met by - or given - she-camels with wings, and on them are saddles of gold, the straps of their sandals, and a light will shine with every step as far as the eye can see. Then they will come to a tree from whose root two springs will spring forth. They will drink from one of them, and it will wash away whatever filth is in their bellies, and they will wash themselves from the other, and their skin and hair will never be disheveled after that, and the freshness of bliss will flow over them. Then they will come to - or they will come to - the gate of Paradise, and there will be a ring of red ruby on gold plates. They will strike the ring on the plate, and a ringing will be heard from above, and every houri will be informed that her husband has arrived, so her guardian will be sent, and it will be opened for him. When she sees him, she will fall down before him.” Maslama said: “I think he said: Prostrating - He says: Raise your head, for I am your guardian and I have been entrusted with your affair. So he follows him and tracks his footsteps. Then the hasty houri will be deceived and come out from the tents of pearls and rubies until she embraces him and says: You are my love and I am your love. I am the immortal one who does not die. I am the gentle one who does not suffer. I am the satisfied one who does not get angry. I am the resident one who does not move. So he enters a house from its foundation to its roof, a distance of one hundred thousand cubits. Its construction is made of pearl stones, with paths of yellow, green, and red in which there is no path that can rival its companion. In the house are seventy beds. On each bed are seventy mattresses. On each mattress are seventy wives. On each wife are seventy garments. The marrow of her leg can be seen from inside the garments. He completes intercourse with her in the space of one of your nights. Rivers flow from beneath them. “Rivers of water unpolluted” - he said: clear, with no turbidity in it - and rivers of milk whose taste never changes - he said: it did not come out of the udders of cattle - and rivers of wine delicious to those who drink - he said: it was not squeezed out by men with their feet. And rivers of purified honey - he said it did not come out of the bellies of bees, he gathers the fruits, if he wishes standing, if he wishes sitting, or if he wishes reclining - then he recited And its shades are drawn low for them, and its fruits are made accessible to them so he desires food and a white bird comes to him, he said or he said green, he said it raises its wings and he eats from its sides whichever color he wishes, then it flies and goes and the angel enters and says: Peace be upon you. This is Paradise, which you have inherited for what you used to do. And if a hair from the hair of the houri fell to the ground, the sun would shine with it black in light. This is a strange hadith and it seems to be mursal, and God knows best.
39:75: When the Almighty mentioned His judgment on the people of Paradise and Hell, and that each one will descend to the place that suits him and is suitable for him, and He is the Just in that, who does not commit injustice, He informed us about His angels that they will surround the Glorious Throne, glorifying and praising their Lord, exalting and magnifying Him, sanctifying Him, and declaring Him free from shortcomings and injustice. He has settled the matter, decided the matter, and ruled with justice. For this reason, the Almighty said, And it will be judged between them, meaning between the creation, in truth. Then He said, And it will be said, ‘Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds,’ meaning the entire universe, its speakers and animals, spoke to God, Lord of the worlds, with praise for His judgment and justice. For this reason, He did not attribute the statement to a speaker, but rather made it absolute, indicating that all of creation bore witness to His praise. Qatada said, “The creation began with praise in His statement, ‘Praise be to God, who created the heavens and the earth,’ and concluded with praise in His statement, the Blessed and Exalted: “And it will be judged between them in truth, and it will be said, ‘Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds.’”
